description: Named comparison sides for tests/run.py (--a, --b). kind oracle: harness.oracle.serve(); kind fixture: the selftest site in tests/fixtures/site/ (fixture:<control> applies a control from tests/fixtures/controls.json); kind command: a server the harness starts in its own process group ({port} and {inspector_port} are free ports, never 8790; {dir} is the target's folder; {log_dir} the run's result folder; an argument "{wrangler}" is the repository's pinned wrangler, npm exec --no -- wrangler, or FEMTO_WRANGLER) and stops with every child; dir: the folder a command serves, which <name>:<path> replaces (dist:<path> serves any built folder exactly like dist); requires: a path that must exist first ({dir} filled in); env: environment variables for the command ({port}, {dir} and {log_dir} filled in). ready: the readiness hook run before collecting (oracle, static, none). max_documents: the most documents one server instance serves; a longer run is split into chunks, each with freshly started servers and browser sessions. build_tag: a tag of this repository that the harness builds first into dir (tests/harness/tagbuild.py: a temporary git worktree of the tag, node build.mjs --out dir, rebuilt when dir/index.html or build.json beside it is missing, the tag's commit or the repository's prismjs version differs from the one build.json records, or dir no longer matches its recorded tree hash; the build holds tests/builds/<tag>.lock exclusively and every server of it holds the lock shared). menu: the menu.json a sections run reads side A's routes and their sections from (a path in the repository; for a build_tag target, the path inside the tag). one_page: the one docs page a sections run loads side B's sections from. comparison: the comparison a pages or sections run is when this target is side A (default pages), which decides the registry entries that apply. same_origin: every document this side serves must load only same-origin resources (PLAN.md criterion 15); a cross-origin load in its Resource Timing entries fails the run outside the diff, where no registry entry applies. See tests/README.md, Modes.

oracle.about: The Remix site at tag remix-final, built with its locked toolchain and served by its own wrangler pages dev (tests/harness/oracle.py).
oracle.max_documents_why: wrangler 4.0.0's InspectorProxyWorker keeps every DevTools event of the worker (Network.enable: several per request) in runtimeMessageBuffer until a DevTools client connects, which none does. Its workerd isolate reached the V8 heap limit (about 1.4 GB) after about 1,240 page loads (43,000 requests) on 2026-10-30 (run p0-gate-self-cf, first attempt). A run therefore restarts every server, with fresh browser sessions, at most every 400 documents per server (tests/README.md, Rig notes).

fixture.about: The harness's selftest site, tests/fixtures/site/. Its sections/ folder is a one-page docs site in miniature for the sections controls: route pages listed in sections/menu.json and the one page sections/docs.html.

dist.same_origin_why: PLAN.md criterion 15: every page loads only same-origin resources. The harness reads each document's own network log (Resource Timing), so a script that only displays a CDN URL passes and a fetch() or inserted <link> to another origin fails, whatever builds the URL.
dist.about: The static site: wrangler pages dev dist (or dist:<path>, any built folder), with the wrangler pinned in package.json. Phase 1 points side B here.
dist.env_why: wrangler writes a debug log on every run; WRANGLER_LOG_PATH keeps it in the run's result folder instead of ~/Library/Preferences/.wrangler/logs.
dist.dir_why: dist:<path> serves another built folder (a relative path is read from the repository root) exactly like dist: the same wrangler, options, readiness and same-origin rule, so several agents can each compare their own build at once.
dist.command_why: {wrangler} is npm exec --no -- wrangler, the wrangler pinned in package.json (--no never downloads one; targets.py checks node_modules/wrangler against the exact pin first). --persist-to gives each server its own state folder in the run's folder, so concurrent servers never share .wrangler/state.
dist.one_page_why: The one docs page (PLAN.md Decision 2): the sections mode's side B loads each section at /docs#<id>, and a color route's at /docs?theme=<color>#version-picker.

static-multipage.same_origin_why: PLAN.md criterion 15: every page loads only same-origin resources. The harness reads each document's own network log (Resource Timing), so a script that only displays a CDN URL passes and a fetch() or inserted <link> to another origin fails, whatever builds the URL.
static-multipage.about: The static site at tag static-multipage (the Phase 1 commit, with the oracle's compiled CSS frozen in site/assets/legacy/), built by the harness into tests/builds/static-multipage/dist and served exactly as dist is. The styles mode's side A (tests/README.md, Modes).
static-multipage.env_why: wrangler writes a debug log on every run; WRANGLER_LOG_PATH keeps it in the run's result folder instead of ~/Library/Preferences/.wrangler/logs.
static-multipage.dir_why: Gitignored (.gitignore: tests/builds/). The folder is the harness's own: a run never builds into dist/, and the build is redone only when the tag moves.
static-multipage.command_why: {wrangler} is npm exec --no -- wrangler, the wrangler pinned in package.json (--no never downloads one; targets.py checks node_modules/wrangler against the exact pin first). --persist-to gives each server its own state folder in the run's folder, so concurrent servers never share .wrangler/state.
static-multipage.build_tag_why: PLAN.md Workflow, 2 Styles: the Phase 2 gate compares the Phase 2 site against the Phase 1 commit, tagged static-multipage. Building the tag, not reading the working tree, keeps side A fixed while the site's CSS changes.

static-femto.about: The static site at tag static-femto (the Phase 2 commit 7587a7e: vendored femto and the five site CSS files, one page per oracle route), built by the harness into tests/builds/static-femto/dist and served exactly as dist is. Side A of Phase 3's comparisons (tests/README.md, Modes): the sections mode's route pages, and a pages run's whole pages.
static-femto.env_why: wrangler writes a debug log on every run; WRANGLER_LOG_PATH keeps it in the run's result folder instead of ~/Library/Preferences/.wrangler/logs.
static-femto.dir_why: Gitignored (.gitignore: tests/builds/). The folder is the harness's own: a run never builds into dist/, and the build is redone only when the tag moves.

static-femto.build_tag_why: PLAN.md Workflow, 3 One page: the Phase 3 gate compares each docs section of the one page against its old route at the Phase 2 commit, tagged static-femto. Building the tag, not reading the working tree, keeps side A fixed while site/ becomes the one page.
static-femto.menu_why: The sections mode maps each old docs route to its section through side A's menu.json, read from the tag (git show static-femto:site/docs/menu.json): its route and variants fields, which Phase 3 removes from the working tree's menu.json.
static-femto.comparison_why: A pages or sections run whose side A is this target is a one-page comparison: only the registry entries whose where.comparisons names one-page apply (and skipped checks), so neither Phase 1's entries (the oracle against the static site) nor Phase 2's (the frozen CSS against femto) hide a difference between the Phase 2 site and the one page (tests/README.md, Divergence registry).

static-one-page.about: The static site at tag static-one-page (the Phase 3 commit 7b90883, "Merge Docs Into One Page": the one docs page, before Phase 4 rewrote the content), built by the harness into tests/builds/static-one-page/dist and served exactly as dist is. Side B of Phase 3's comparisons when they are rerun between the tags (tests/owner-safari.sh parity): the sections mode's one page, and a pages run's whole pages.

static-one-page.build_tag_why: PLAN.md Workflow, 3 One page: Phase 3's gate compared the one page at that phase's commit against static-femto. From Phase 4 dist/ describes femto 3 and matches neither, so criterion 2's Safari legs are rerun between the commits the gates compared: static-femto against this tag, the Phase 3 commit (the owner, 2026-11-06). Building the tag, not reading the working tree, keeps side B fixed.
static-one-page.one_page_why: The one docs page at the Phase 3 commit (PLAN.md Decision 2): the sections mode's side B loads each section at /docs#<id>, and a color route's at /docs?theme=<color>#version-picker, as it did from dist at Phase 3's gate.
